input: When the results reported for the benchmark material are placed side by side, it becomes apparent that the two groups' selectivity values cannot both be an accurate description of the same solid operating under the same conditions, and the divergence between them appears to track the test conditions considerably more closely than it tracks the material itself. The higher values were obtained from equilibrium measurements performed on samples that had been activated under vacuum and held at each point until the reading had fully stabilised, whereas the lower values emerged from mixture breakthrough tests, in which selectivity is inferred from the separation actually achieved rather than measured at equilibrium, and in which a slow approach to equilibrium within the pores can easily masquerade as a weaker separation. The IAST predictions that have been offered in support of each position do little to arbitrate between them, since the single-component isotherms on which those predictions rest were themselves measured under the two different regimes. On the basis of the evidence as it currently stands, the benchmark material would appear to be preferred where the feed is dry and the contact time is long, these being the conditions under which the equilibrium values were obtained, while under short-contact conditions the preference remains unestablished, and the breakthrough results continue to stand, unrefuted, on their own ground.
target: Against the benchmark material, the two groups' selectivity values cannot both describe the same solid under the same conditions, and the difference between them tracks the test conditions more closely than it tracks the material. The higher values come from equilibrium measurements on samples activated under vacuum and held at each point until the reading steadied. The lower values come from mixture breakthrough tests, where the selectivity is inferred from the separation achieved rather than measured at equilibrium, and where a slow approach to equilibrium in the pores reads as a weaker separation. IAST predictions widen rather than settle the difference, because the single-component isotherms fed to IAST were themselves taken under the two regimes. On the evidence as it stands, the benchmark material is preferred where the feed is dry and the contact time is long, the conditions under which the equilibrium values were obtained; under short contact the preference is not established, and the breakthrough results stand unrefuted on their own ground, which is the ground any short-contact design would actually work on, with residence times set by the bed and the flow rather than by the patience of the measurement
